title: Power-on to login on the i.MX 8M Plus

steps.title: Six stages, each loading the next
steps.body:
Read the chain left to right and top to bottom: every card is one stage of the boot, with where it runs, what it does and which file this repository builds for it.

Each stage either finishes and exits, or stays in memory to serve the next one. The coloured bands mark the **secure world** (privileged firmware) and the **normal world** (U-Boot, Linux).

steps.title: 1 · The Boot ROM is fixed in silicon
steps.body:
Code burned into the chip that runs first, at the highest privilege level (EL3). It reads the boot-mode switch, loads `imx-boot` from the card at 32 KiB, checks its header and starts the SPL.

There is nothing to build here, and it decides where your first loader must sit on the storage.

steps.title: 2 · The SPL brings DDR memory to life
steps.body:
The SPL (Secondary Program Loader) is a small first part of U-Boot that runs from on-chip RAM at `0x0092_0000`. It reads the SoM EEPROM, trains the LPDDR4 memory with NXP's training firmware, and loads the FIT image holding BL31 and U-Boot.

Without working DRAM nothing later can run, so a fault here usually means a silent board.

steps.title: 3 · BL31 is the secure monitor that never leaves
steps.body:
TF-A (Trusted Firmware-A) BL31 sits at `0x0097_0000` in on-chip RAM at EL3. It handles every SMC (a call from the normal world into secure firmware), programs the TZASC, CSU and RDC protection units, and implements PSCI for CPU on/off and reset.

Linux cannot start its other CPUs without it.

steps.title: 4 · OP-TEE is optional and not in this build
steps.body:
OP-TEE is a trusted OS at S-EL1 that would run Trusted Applications for keys, crypto and secure storage from DDR at `0x5600_0000`. The dashed card means it is not part of the default build yet.

If it were added, BL31 would enter it before handing over to U-Boot.

steps.title: 5 · U-Boot proper picks the kernel and device tree
steps.body:
The full U-Boot runs at EL2 in the normal world from `0x4020_0000`. It chooses the right DTB (device tree, the hardware description) for the detected module, loads `/boot/Image.gz`, sets the kernel arguments and calls `booti`.

BL31 enters it with an ERET, the instruction that drops privilege from EL3 to EL2.

steps.title: 6 · Linux takes over and starts the other CPUs
steps.body: The kernel runs at EL1 with applications at EL0, from `0x4060_0000`. It asks BL31 through PSCI to start three more CPUs, mounts `mmcblk1p1` as the root filesystem and runs `/sbin/init`, which ends at the login prompt.

steps.anchor: STILL IN MEMORY WHILE LINUX RUNS
steps.title: What survives after boot
steps.body:
The Boot ROM and SPL are finished and their on-chip RAM is reused. U-Boot is gone after `booti`.

Only BL31 stays at EL3 for good, serving PSCI and the i.MX SiP calls (DDR frequency, CPU frequency, power domains); OP-TEE would stay too, reached through BL31.

anchor: Dashed = optional stage, not part of the default build. Red arrows = transitions owned by the secure monitor.
steps.title: Takeaway: the secure monitor owns the handoffs
steps.body: Red arrows are transitions that BL31 performs, so the secure monitor is involved from the first handoff to the last power-off. Each stage exists because the one before it cannot do the job: ROM cannot train DRAM, the SPL cannot fit a full bootloader, and U-Boot cannot run Linux's drivers.
